facts.fact: Liberia's Deputy Minister for Planning, Research and Development states that the September 2025 EMIS peer review in Monrovia produced a costed three-year EMIS Action Plan of USD 4.5 million, one of whose six priority areas is introducing a unique national Learner and Teacher ID system.
facts.system: National Learner and Teacher ID system

facts.fact: The Deputy Minister states that the three-year EMIS Action Plan endorses a financing framework in which the Government of Liberia contributes 60 per cent of the USD 4.5 million and development partners 40 per cent; this is the plan's framework for all six priority areas, not a budget line shown for the learner ID system.
facts.system: National Learner and Teacher ID system

facts.fact: The Deputy Minister states that the EMIS process was led by government leaders, statisticians, planners, ICT teams and regional officers rather than by donors, and that the national team co-designed the roadmap that includes unique learner and teacher IDs.
facts.system: National Learner and Teacher ID system

systems.owner: Ministry of Education (Deputy Minister for Planning, Research and Development)
systems.tiers: National, with county focal points; counties short of computers, internet and dashboards
More than 6,000 schools and nearly 1.5 million learners; the 2024-2025 census was the first since 2022

systems.system: National Learner and Teacher ID system
systems.country_label: unique national Learner and Teacher ID system

note: The EMIS as described is the annual school census; the facts are for the planned learner ID system only. The 2024-2025 census, the first since 2022, is a census event and gives no fact.
